(a) Incorporation in construction. Every officer, board, department, commission or agency of the city charged with the duty of preparing specifications, or awarding or entering into contracts for the design, erection or construction of buildings or other structures, including additions to existing structures, for the city shall incorporate or cause to be incorporated in such buildings or other structures protection from radioactive fallout for at least its normal anticipated occupancy which shall meet or exceed the minimum space and protection criteria recommended by the Defense Civil Preparedness Agency, United States Department of Defense, unless exempted from such shelter requirements in accordance with subsection (b) of this section.
(b) Exemptions. The city council may exempt buildings or other structures from the requirements of subsection (a) of this section where it finds that the addition of fallout protection will create, in the building or other structure, an additional net cost in excess of three percent in the construction of such building or that other factors make it unnecessary or impracticable to incorporate fallout protection in the design or construction of such building or structure.
(c) Purpose of requirements. It shall be the policy of the city council that fallout shelter protection shall be incorporated into all city buildings or structures to the fullest extent practicable in order to provide protection against the effect of radioactive fallout for the greatest possible number of people in the event of nuclear attack upon the United States or an accidental nuclear explosion.
(Code 1967, § 2-19; Ord. No. 134, §§ 1—3, 12-4-1973)

In addition to any and all powers enumerated in the city Charter and Code, the mayor, as the chief executive of the city, shall have the further emergency powers as follows:
(1) The mayor shall have the right to declare an emergency when, in his opinion, one or more of the following conditions exist:
a. There is extreme likelihood of danger of destruction of life or property due to unusual conditions.
b. Unusual or extreme weather conditions, making use of city streets or areas difficult or impossible.
c. Civil unrest, commotion or uprising is imminent or exists.
d. There is a stoppage or loss of electrical power affecting a major portion of the city.
(2) After declaration of such emergency the mayor, as chief executive, shall have the right to exercise the power to:
a. Use employees of the city to assist in the safety and preservation of life, limb and property of citizenry of the city.
b. Close streets and sidewalks and delineate areas within the city wherein an emergency exists.
c. Impose emergency curfew regulations.
d. Close business establishments within the affected area.
e. Close any and all municipally owned buildings and other facilities to the use of the general public.
f. Do any and all acts necessary and incidental to the preservation of life, limb and property of the citizenry of the city.
(3) No emergency as set forth in this section may be effective for more than 72 hours after the declaration of an emergency by the mayor. However, upon declaration of a second or further emergency to exist, the emergency powers as set forth in this section may be exercised during such further emergency period, but never for more than 72 hours in one declared emergency period.
(4) No emergency period shall extend beyond the next regular, special or called meeting of the mayor and council.
(5) The declaration of an emergency as to a portion of the city shall specify with exactness the area in which the emergency is declared to exist.

The City of Moultrie, Georgia (the "employer") established a retirement plan for employees of the City of Moultrie effective January 1, 1966 (the "plan") and the employer hereby amends and restates the plan effective January 1, 2015 through which will be provided retirement and other benefits to the city's employees through a trust fund established for that purpose. This plan is considered to be in the public interest in attracting and retaining better qualified personnel in the city's service and in providing greater personal security to its employees in their old age. This plan is intended to provide a governmental qualified defined benefit pension plan under Internal Revenue Code Section 401(a) and 414(d). The benefits described in the plan are provided for the exclusive benefit of the participants and their beneficiaries. The plan shall be maintained at city hall. 270:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Accrued benefit means the retirement income to which a participant will be entitled at his normal retirement age, based upon the actual number of years of service completed by the participant as of the date of determination and his compensation (if applicable) in those years of service.
Actuarial equivalent or actuarial equivalence means, with respect to a benefit calculated under this plan, any benefit that has the same present value on the date the benefit payment commences, using a seven percent interest rate per annum and the unisex mortality table in effect on the date benefits commence, as proscribed by the Commissioner of the Internal Revenue Service for purposes of Code Section 417(e)(3). Effective prior to January 1, 2010, the plan used a seven percent interest rate per annum and a 50 percent and 50 percent blend of the 1983 Group Annuity Table for males and females.
Authorized leave of absence means any temporary layoff or any absence authorized by the employer under the employer's standard personnel practices provided that all persons under similar circumstances must be treated alike in the granting of such authorized leaves of absence and provided further that the participant returns within the period of authorized absence. An absence due to service in the Armed Forces of the United States shall be considered an authorized leave of absence to the extent required by federal law.
Average monthly compensation means the average of the participant's compensation over the 36 consecutive months within the most recent ten-year period of service which produces the highest such average; provided however if an employee has not been employed continuously in service, his separate periods of service will be aggregated for purposes of this section as if he has been employed in service continuously during such aggregated period. If the employee's aggregated period of service is less than three years as of his date of termination of employment, his average monthly compensation will be determined as his average monthly compensation for his entire period of service. The following rules shall be applied to determine a participant's average monthly compensation:
(1) Only compensation earned or deemed to have been earned during a period for which the participant is receiving service or is an eligible employee may be counted towards average monthly compensation.
(2) Compensation shall be counted in the year paid, even if earned in a prior year.
(3) Only compensation earned or deemed to have been earned before January 1, 2018, may be counted towards average monthly compensation. No compensation earned on or after January 1, 2018, shall be taken into account in determining a participant's accrued benefit under the plan.
Beneficiary means any individual(s), trust, estate or other entity or entities designated by the participant in accordance with procedures established by the plan administrator to receive any death benefits under the plan. Any beneficiary designation shall be void if the participant revokes the designation. If a married participant fails to designate a beneficiary, or if the designated non-spouse primary beneficiary fails to survive the participant and the participant has not designated a contingent beneficiary, or if both the designated non-spouse primary beneficiary and contingent beneficiary fail to survive the participant, the beneficiary shall be (a) the participant's eligible spouse, or; (b) if no eligible spouse is alive, the participant's eligible dependent(s), or (c) if no eligible dependents, the participant's estate. If an unmarried participant fails to designate a beneficiary, or if the designated beneficiary fails to survive the participant and the participant has not designated a contingent beneficiary, or if both the designated beneficiary and contingent beneficiary fail to survive the participant, the beneficiary shall be the participant's eligible dependents, if any, and if none, the participant's estate.
For the purposes of this section, revocation of prior beneficiary designations will occur when a participant files a new valid designation with the plan administrator.
Nothing in this definition of beneficiary shall be interpreted to allow a participant to designate a beneficiary, or to be entitled to a death benefit, that is not otherwise provided under the terms of this plan.
Board means the board of trustees of the plan.
City means the City of Moultrie, Georgia.
Code means the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. A reference to a specific provision of the Code shall include such provision and any applicable Treasury Regulation pertaining thereto.
Compensation means the basic salary or wage paid to the employee by the employer, which is subject to withholding for purposes of federal income taxes plus amounts not includible in the gross income of the employee by reason of Code Sections 125, 402(e)(3), 402(h)(1)(B) 403(b), 414(h), 457(h) and effective July 1, 2003, Code section 132(f)(4); provided however, compensation will not include bonuses, overtime pay, expense allowances, or any other irregular or special compensation payments.
Except with respect to qualified participants (as defined below), in no event shall the compensation of a participant taken into account under the plan for any plan year exceed (i)$200,000.00 for plan years beginning on or after January 1, 1989, (ii) $150,000.00 for plan years on or after the later of (a) January 1, 1996 or (b) the 90th day after the opening of the first legislative session that begins on or after January 1, 1996, or (iii) for plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2002, the limitations of Code Section 401(a)(17) in effect as of the beginning of the plan year (i.e., $265,000.00 for 2015). For purposes of applying the $150,000.00 limit for the 1996 plan year, if any employee is the spouse or a lineal descendant of an employee (provided the lineal descendant is younger than age 19 by the end of the plan year) who is one of the ten "highly compensated employees" (within the meaning of Code Section 414(q)) paid the greatest amount of earnings (determined without regard to the $150,000.00 limit, as adjusted) during the plan year, the employee shall not be treated as a separate employee.
The limitations set forth in the preceding paragraph shall be subject to adjustment annually as provided in Code Section 401(a)(17)(B) and Code Section 415(d); provided, however, that the dollar increase in effect on January 1 of any calendar year, if any, is effective for the plan year.
The limit described in the previous paragraphs shall not apply to any qualified participant. A qualified participant is any participant who first became a participant in the plan before January 1, 1996.
The plan year limitations in effect as of the beginning of the plan year in which each 12-month period used to determine average monthly compensation begins shall apply to compensation paid during such 12-month period.
Disability or disabled means the participant is or would be entitled to disability retirement benefits under the federal Social Security Act.
Early retirement age means (1) the date the participant has both attained age 55 and accrued 15 or more years of service; or (2) the date the participant's age plus his number of years of service equals 80 or more.
Early retirement date shall mean the date as of which the participant actually commences his retirement income that is the first day of any month after the participant has attained his early retirement age but before his normal retirement age.
Effective date means January 1, 2015, the effective date of this amendment and restatement. The plan was originally effective as of January 1, 1966.
Eligible dependent means a minor unmarried child (natural or adopted) of the participant or any child (natural or adopted) regardless of age, who because of physical or mental impairment and is dependent on the participant or the eligible spouse for substantially all his maintenance or support.
Eligible employee means any full-time employee other than the following:
(a) Employees who are regularly scheduled to work less than 35 hours per week or six months per year;
(b) Temporary employees;
(c) A nonresident alien who receives no earned income from an employer which constitutes income from sources within the United States;
(d) A leased employee;
(e) An employee classified by the employer as a leased employee, regardless of whether such employee is a leased employee within the meaning of Code Section 414(n)(2); or
(f) A person who is initially classified by the employer as an independent contractor or leased employee for purposes of the withholding and payment of employment taxes, even if such person is later determined, whether by the employer or otherwise, to be a common law employee of the employer.
(g) Effective January 1, 2018, no employee shall be eligible to participate in the plan if not already actively participating as of December 31, 2017.
Eligible spouse means, as of any applicable date, a person who was married to the participant on the earlier of the date of the participant's death or the date payment of the participant's retirement income commenced; provided, however, for purposes of section 2-150 and the pre-retirement survivor annuity, eligible spouse means the person who was married to the participant continuously during the one-year immediately preceding the participant's death.
Employee means any person employed by the employer as a common law employee, any person on authorized leave of absence from the employer, and any person who is a leased employee.
Employer means the City of Moultrie, Georgia.
Employment means the service of an employee with the employer.
Entry date means the first day of the calendar month coincident with or next following the completion of six months of full-time employment with the employer.
Fiduciary means any party named as a fiduciary in article 10 of the plan. Any party shall be considered a fiduciary of the plan only to the extent of the powers and duties specifically allocated to such party under the plan.
Full-time employee means a permanent employee who is regularly scheduled to work at least 35 hours per week.
Fund means the money and other properties held and administered by the board of trustee(s).
Interest means the interest credited on participant contributions. Interest shall be compounded annually at five percent. Interest shall stop accruing as of the date that this plan is terminated.
Late retirement date means, for a participant who continues his employment beyond his normal retirement date, the first day of the month coincident with or immediately following such participant's termination of employment.
Leased employee means any person who is described in Code Section 414(n)(2), which defines leased employee to mean any individual who provides services to an employer if:
(1) Such services are provided pursuant to an agreement between an employer and any other person;
(2) Such person has performed such services for an employer (or for an employer and related persons) on a substantially full-time basis for a period of at least one year; and
(3) Such services are performed under the primary direction or control of an employer.
Normal form means a monthly retirement income payable as a life annuity which ceases upon the participant's death.
Normal retirement age means the normal full retirement age at which the employee can receive 100 percent social security benefits based in the person's year of birth.
Normal retirement date means the first day of the month coincident with or next following the participant's normal retirement age.
Other rules. A defined term, such as "retirement," will normally govern the definitions of derivatives therefrom, such as "retire," even though such derivatives are not specifically defined and even if they are or are not initially capitalized. Singular and plural nouns and pronouns shall be interchangeable as the factual context may allow or require. The words "hereof," "herein," "hereunder" and other similar compounds of the word "here" shall mean and refer to the entire plan and not to any particular provision or section.
Parental leave means an absence from work because of the pregnancy of the employee, the birth of a child of the employee or the placement of a child with the employee in connection with the adoption of that child by the employee, or for purposes of caring for that child for a period beginning immediately following such birth or placement.
Participant means a person who is actively an employee who is or becomes eligible to participate in the plan as provided in section 2-148.
Participant contribution means the amount that participants contribute to the plan through salary reduction in accordance with section 2-153(b) of the plan.
Plan or plan and trust means the retirement plan and trust for the employees of the City of Moultrie.
Plan administrator or administrator means the employer or an individual or individuals or a committee designated by the employer for purposes of conducting the day to day activities of the plan.
Plan year means the 12-month period from October 1 through September 30th except as follows:
(1) For periods prior to January 1, 1986, the plan year was the calendar year.
(2) January 1, 1986 through September 30, 1986 was a short plan year.
Pre-retirement survivor annuity means as defined in section 2-150.
Qualified military leave means the period of an employee's leave of absence for active duty for training and service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines, or Coast Guard of the United States of America (or any Reserve or National Guard components thereof when engaged in active duty training, inactive duty training, or full-time National Guard duty) and the commissioned corps of the United States Public Health Service or any other category of persons designated by the President of the United States in a time of war or emergency, but only if the employee was employed in service of the employer immediately preceding the leave and the employee:
(1) Returns to service no later than seven days after the termination of active duty of 30 days or less duration;
(2) Applies in writing for service within 14 days after the termination of active duty of 31 to 181 days duration;

Retirement or retirement date means the date on which the participant actually ceases employment for early retirement, normal retirement, or late retirement, whichever is applicable.
Retirement income means any amount payable to or on behalf of a participant, beneficiary or eligible spouse in accordance with the provisions of the plan.
Service means the measurement of a participant's employment with the employer that is used to determine the amount of his benefits under the plan, vesting and eligibility. Service shall be all years and completed months (but not partial months) during which an individual is an eligible employee under this plan and is receiving compensation from the employer or is on an authorized leave of absence or qualified military leave, subject to the following rules:
(a) Service shall not be granted for periods during which the employee is not an eligible employee;
(b) Service shall not be granted for any time prior to January 1, 1983;
(c) Service shall not be granted for any period during which the eligible employee fails to make required participant contributions;
(d) Service shall be granted for the time period between the eligible employee's first date of hire and the eligible employee's entry date; and
(e) Partial years of service shall be credited in increments of one-twelfth of a year, with one calendar month equal to one-twelfth of a year.
Spouse means the person to whom the participant is legally married under the laws of the State of Georgia, except that, effective as of June 26, 2015, the term "spouse" means the person to whom the participant is legally married. (b) Discharge from the service of the employer; or,
(c) Death.

Treasury regulation means regulations pertaining to certain Code Sections as issued by the Secretary of the Treasury.
Trust fund means the trust or any other pool of assets established by the employer to hold assets that will be applied to fund the benefits under the plan.
Trustee means the persons appointed by the governing authority to be members of the board that oversees the trust fund.

(1) Entry date. An eligible employee shall first become a participant as of the first day of the month coincident with or next following the completion of six month of service with the employer.

(3) Cessation of participation. A participant shall cease participation in the plan as of the date on which the employee no longer meets the definition of eligible employee or upon his termination of employment.

See section 2-149(d)(3) for provisions regarding the disposition of the accrued benefit of a non-vested participant upon a termination of employment.
(2) Rehire of employee with less than ten years of service. An eligible employee who was a participant in this plan, had fewer than ten years of service at the time of his termination of employment, received a distribution of his participant contributions plus interest and who is subsequently rehired by the employer, shall be treated as a new employee upon rehire, unless he or she repays to the plan all amounts received from the plan after termination of employment.
(3) Rehire of employee with more than ten years of service. An eligible employee who was a participant in this plan, had ten years of service or more at the time of his termination of employment and who is subsequently rehired by an employer, shall have all his service restored; provided however, if prior to rehire, the participant received all amounts due under the plan, service shall not be restored unless the participant repays to the plan all of the amounts received plus interest.

(a) Normal retirement.
(1) Amount. A participant who retires on his normal retirement date shall be entitled to a monthly retirement income paid in the normal form equal to:
a. The participant's monthly pension amount as determined as of December 31, 1982, plus
b. One and six-tenths percent of the participant's average monthly compensation multiplied by the participant's service.
c. For purposes of determining a participant's monthly pension amount, no compensation or service shall be taken into account after December 31, 2017. However, service earned after such date shall continue to be counted for purposes of vesting under the plan and for purpose of determining eligibility for early retirement.
(2) Vesting on normal retirement. A participant who attains normal retirement age while in active employment with an employer shall become 100 percent vested in his accrued benefit as of such date.
(3) Normal form. Retirement income shall be expressed as a monthly amount, payable as an annuity for the participant's life (the "normal form").
(b) Early retirement.
(1) Eligibility. Each participant who retires on or after his early retirement age but before his normal retirement age, may elect early retirement. A participant who elects early retirement is entitled to receive a monthly retirement income payable in the form described in section 2-151 beginning on his early retirement date.
(2) Amount of early retirement income. The retirement income payable to a participant who elects early retirement shall be determined in the same manner as his normal retirement benefit calculated as described above, but reduced by zero and five-twelfths percent for each month by which the participant's early retirement date precedes his normal retirement date to take into account the participant's younger age and the earlier commencement of retirement income payments.
(3) Rule of 80. Notwithstanding section (b)(1) above, effective between September 30, 2016 and March 31, 2017 only, the retirement income payable to a participant who retires before his normal retirement age but on or after the age at which the sum of the participant's age plus his number of years of service equals 80 or more, shall be determined in the same manner as his normal retirement benefit calculated as described above, unreduced.
(c) Late retirement date.
(1) Eligibility. Any participant who attains his normal retirement age may remain in the active employ of the employer beyond his normal retirement age and may postpone his retirement income payments until a later date; provided however, that a participant may not postpone receipt of his retirement income beyond the required beginning date as set forth in section 2-151(e). Such retirement shall be known as the participant's late retirement date and is payable in the form described in section 2-151.
(2) Amount of late retirement income. The retirement income payable to a participant who retires on his late retirement date shall be the sum of a., b. and c. defined below:
a. The participant's normal retirement income; and
b. An actuarial adjustment for the plan year which includes the participant's normal retirement date and each plan year thereafter as determined in (3) below; and
c. The excess, if any of the additional benefit accrual earned after the participant's normal retirement date during the plan year which includes his normal retirement date and during each plan year thereafter, over the actuarial adjustment for each such plan year respectively.
(3) Actuarial adjustment. The actuarial adjustment will be determined as of the close of each plan year and will be equal to the increase in the participant's monthly retirement income as of the close of the preceding plan year (or the participant's normal retirement date, if later) which is required in order to provide a monthly benefit as of the determination date that is the actuarial equivalent of the monthly benefit as of the close of the preceding plan year (or the participant's normal retirement date, if later).
(d) Vested termination benefit.
(1) Ten year cliff vesting provision. A participant who terminates employment for any reason other than retirement but after completing ten years of service shall be entitled to the monthly retirement income equal to the normal retirement income earned by the participant determined in accordance with section 2-149(a) hereof but using the participant's compensation and service as of his termination of employment. Such benefit shall be referred to herein as a vested termination benefit and shall be payable in the form described in section 2-151. A participant who terminates employment with the employer for any reason other than retirement and before completing ten years of service shall not be entitled to receive any retirement income under this plan (other than a return of participant contributions as provided in (3) below).
(2) Commencement of retirement income for vested terminated participants.
a. Commencement at normal retirement age. A vested terminated participant's retirement income shall commence as of his normal retirement date, unless the participant is eligible for and elects early commencement of his retirement income as provided in b. below.
b. Commencement before or after normal retirement age. A terminated participant generally may elect to convert his vested termination benefit into an early retirement income or late retirement income which is payable either before or after his normal retirement date, respectively, in accordance with section 2-149(b) and section 2-149(c), provided he has met any age or service requirement set forth therein.
(3) Return of contributions. If a participant has a termination of employment before earning at least ten years of service he shall receive a mandatory distribution of his participant contributions, plus interest. If such participant contributions plus interest are less than $5,000.00, they shall be returned to the participant in a single lump sum payment as of his termination of employment or as soon as practical thereafter. If such participant contributions plus interest are equal to or greater than $5,000.00, they shall be returned to the participant in a single lump sum payment as of the one-year anniversary of the participant's termination of employment or as soon as practical thereafter. If a participant has a termination of employment at least 15 years prior to his normal retirement age, the participant will receive a one-time election to receive an immediate lump sum distribution of his participant contributions, plus interest and forgo any other benefits under the plan, upon such termination of employment. Such distribution shall be made within 90 days of the termination of employment or as soon as practical thereafter.
(4) Forfeiture. Benefits under the plan may be reduced or forfeited to the extent permitted under O.C.G.A. §§ 47-1-20 through 47-1-25, if the participant is convicted of a public employment, drug related or other covered crime.
(e) Disability. A participant who terminates employment due to a disability, after completing ten years of service, shall receive a monthly retirement income equal to the normal retirement income determined as of his termination of employment beginning as of the first day of the month following his determination of disability. Such disability benefit may be paid in an optional form, as elected by the participant in accordance with section 2-151(c) of the plan.
(f) Restoration of service.
(1) Reemployment before becoming vested. If a participant has a termination of employment before earning at least ten years of service and is rehired by an employer, his years of service attributable to the previous period of employment shall be ignored unless he repays within one year of rehire all participant contributions plus interest that he received from the plan.
(2) Reemployment after becoming vested. If a participant has a termination of employment after earning at least ten years of service and is rehired by an employer, his years of service attributable to the previous period of employment shall be restored unless prior to rehire, the participant received all amounts due under the plan. In such a case, if the participant repays the entire distribution plus interest to the plan within one year of rehire, all his years of service shall be restored.

(a) Pre-retirement survivor annuity. If a participant's employment terminates on account of his death after he is eligible for a vested termination benefit, an early retirement income, normal retirement income or late retirement income, but before benefits have begun, his eligible spouse or eligible dependents(s) shall be eligible to receive a monthly retirement income known as a pre-retirement survivor annuity. A participant who attains at least age 55 prior to his death may make an election to have the pre-retirement survivor annuity paid to his or her beneficiary in an amount equal to the survivor portion of a 50 percent joint and survivor annuity, or the survivor portion of a 100 percent joint and survivor annuity. If a participant has made no such election prior to his death then the pre-retirement survivor annuity shall equal 50 percent of the monthly retirement income the participant would have received if he terminated employment the date before his death. Pre-retirement death benefits shall be payable as of the first day of each month coincident or next following the participant's date of death and shall be payable to the eligible spouse or to the eligible dependent(s) in equal shares to each eligible dependent.
(b) Return of participant contributions. If a participant dies before meeting the requirements of section 2-150(a) above, his designated beneficiary shall be entitled to receive a lump sum payment equal to his participant contributions plus interest.
(c) Death after retirement. If a participant's employment terminates on account of his death after his retirement income has commenced in the normal form, the participant's designated beneficiary shall receive a benefit equal to the excess of any of the total participant contributions plus interest over the total payments made to the participant as of his date of death. If a participant's employment terminates on account of his death after his retirement income has commenced in an optional form, his beneficiary shall receive the benefits determined under the option selected.

(a) Payment of retirement income.
(1) Monthly payments. The retirement income payable for normal, early or late retirement shall be payable on the first day of each month and shall begin on the normal, early or late retirement date as applicable; provided however, a participant will not be considered to have retired and will not be eligible to commence receipt of benefits of his early retirement income as long as he continues to be employed by the employer or if he is reemployed by the employer (prior to his normal retirement date) within 90 days of his termination of employment.
(2) Benefit commencement date. Normal, early or late retirement income payments shall not commence earlier that the first day of the month following the date on which the participant's complete application for a benefit is filed at the office of the plan administrator; provided however, payment must commence by the required beginning date.
(3) Death of participant before payments begin. If a participant dies before his retirement income payments are effective, no benefits shall be payable under the plan except as provided in section 2-150.
(b) Normal form of payment. The normal form of payment shall be a life annuity option, which is a monthly retirement income payable to the participant during the participant's lifetime, with payments ceasing upon the participant's death. All benefit formulas in this plan shall give the amount of the participant's retirement income if it is paid in the life annuity option, beginning at the participant's normal retirement date.
(c) Optional forms of payment.
(1) Optional forms available. A participant may elect to receive any of the optional forms of payment listed below, in lieu of the normal form of payment. The selection of an optional form of benefit shall be final and binding upon the participant and his beneficiary on the date the participant's retirement income commences, except as otherwise provided below.
a. One hundred and twenty months certain and life option. This is a reduced monthly retirement income equal to the actuarial equivalent of the life annuity option. The retirement income shall be payable to the participant during his lifetime and, in the event of the participant's death within a period of 120 months after the commencement of benefits, the same monthly amount shall be payable to the participant's beneficiary for the remainder of such 120 month period.
b. Joint and survivor annuity option. This is a reduced monthly retirement income equal to the actuarial equivalent of the life annuity option. The retirement income shall be payable to the participant for his life, and upon the participant's death, a designated percentage (100 percent, 66 ⅔ percent, 50 percent as elected by the participant) of the participant's retirement income shall be payable to the participant's beneficiary for the beneficiary's life. Such retirement income shall cease on the later of the death of the participant or the death of the participant's beneficiary.
c. Death of beneficiary. If the participant's beneficiary or joint annuitant dies before the participant's retirement income begins, any optional form elected by the participant will be cancelled and the participant will receive retirement income in the normal form unless the participant makes a new election for an optional form with a new beneficiary or joint annuitant.
d. Social Security option. This is an increased monthly retirement income equal to the actuarial equivalent of the life annuity option. The retirement income shall be payable to the participant for his life until his social security benefits commence and a reduced retirement income payable thereafter for his life, so that combined social security benefits and retirement income payments are essentially level.
e. Death [of] the participant and beneficiary. If both the participant and the beneficiary die after the date the participant's retirement income payment becomes effective but before full payment has been made, any guaranteed payment shall be paid to a contingent beneficiary and if the commuted value of the remaining payments is less than $5,000.00, such payment shall automatically be made in a lump sum.
(2) Lump sum option. If the present value of the total amount due to the participant or beneficiary is $10,000.00 or less, the participant or beneficiary may elect to receive payment in a single lump sum payment.
(3) Minimum distribution incidental benefit rules. Any optional form of benefit elected by the participant must comply with the minimum distribution incidental benefit requirement of proposed Treasury Regulation § 1.401(a)(9)-2. This rule insures that the retirement benefits payable under the plan are more than incidental.
(d) Small lump sum payments. If the monthly amount of the total retirement income (including that of a pre-retirement survivor annuity or disability payment) to be paid is less than $100.00 per month as of the date the retirement income payments are first effective or as of the date of death of the participant, then the single sum actuarial equivalent of such retirement income shall be paid in a lump sum to the participant or beneficiary, as applicable without their consent.
(e) Special distribution rules (including age 70½ rules).
(1) Commencement of distribution at normal retirement age. Payment of retirement income shall commence no later than the 60th day after the latest of the close of the plan year in which occurs:
a. The participant's 65 birthday;
b. The tenth anniversary of the date the participant commenced participation in this plan; or
c. The participant's termination of employment.
(2) Commencement at required beginning date. Notwithstanding (e)(1) above, distribution to a participant shall commence not later than the Required beginning date. The required beginning date shall be April 1 of the calendar year following the later of (i) the calendar year in which the participant attains age 70½ or (ii) the calendar year in which the participant terminates employment.
(3) Effective date. The rules set forth in this section 2-151(e) shall apply for purposes of determining the required minimum distribution to participants and designated beneficiaries (as defined below) for calendar years beginning on and after January 1, 2003 even if, in the case of a designated beneficiary, the participant died before 2003.
(4) No extension of death benefits or payment forms. Nothing in this section 2-151(e) shall be deemed to extend any death benefit or permit any beneficiary designation or payment form not otherwise provided or permitted under this plan. This section 2-151(e) shall, instead, be deemed to limit and modify any provision of this plan to the extent that such limitation or modification is necessary to ensure that the plan complies with this section 2-151(e), Code Section 401(a)(9) and the regulations thereunder.
For purposes of this section 2-151(e), distributions are considered to begin on the participant's required beginning date. If annuity payments irrevocably commence to the Participant before the participant's required beginning date, or to the participant's spouse before the date distributions are required to begin to the surviving spouse under section 2-151(e)(7)b below, the date distributions are considered to begin is the date distributions actually commence.
(5) Period of distribution. The entire interest of each participant in this plan will be distributed, beginning not later than the required beginning date described in paragraph (2) above, over the life of such participant or over the lives of such participant and his or her designated beneficiary, or over a period not extending beyond the life expectancy of such participant or the life expectancy of such participant and his or her designated beneficiary.
(6) Death of participant after distribution has begun. If distribution of a participant's interest has begun in accordance with paragraph (2) above (i.e., distributions on or after the required beginning date), and if the participant dies before his entire interest has been distributed to him, then the remaining portion of such interest will be distributed at least as rapidly as under the method of distribution being used under paragraph (2) as of the date of the participant's death.
(7) Death of participant before distribution has begun. If a participant dies before distribution of the participant's interest has begun in accordance with paragraph (2) above (i.e., no distributions have been made on or after the required beginning date), the entire interest of the participant must be paid over whichever of the following periods is applicable:
a. If one or more designated beneficiary(ies) is not the participant's spouse, the distribution period shall be the designated beneficiary's remaining life expectancy.
b. If the sole designated beneficiary is the participant's spouse, the distribution period shall be the spouse's remaining life expectancy.
c. If there is no designated beneficiary, the entire account shall be distributed by the end of the calendar year that includes the fifth anniversary of the participant's death.
Distributions under this subsection (e)(7) shall commence as follows:
i. Distributions under 2-151(e)(7)(a.), (i.e., distribution to a non-spouse designated beneficiary) shall begin on or before the end of the calendar year that begins immediately after the calendar year in which the participant died.
ii. Distributions under section 2-151(e)(7)(b.) (i.e., distribution solely to a spousal designated beneficiary) shall begin on or before the later of the end of the calendar year immediately following the calendar year in which the participant died and the end of the calendar year in which the participant would have attained age 70½.
(8) Form of distribution. For a participant who is employed by an employer after his required beginning date, any distribution payable under this section 2-151(e) may be paid in any optional form of benefit that is available under the plan, provided that all consent requirements under the plan are satisfied. Any form of distribution payable under this plan, however, must satisfy the following requirements:
a. The distribution must be in the form of a periodic annuity for the participant's life, or for the joint life expectancy of the participant and designated beneficiary or over a period certain that does not exceed the maximum length of the period certain determined under the regulations.
b. The interval between payments must be uniform over the entire distribution period and must not exceed one year.
c. If payments have commenced over a period certain, the period certain may not be changed.
d. Distributions in the form of a life annuity must satisfy the minimum distribution incidental benefit (MDIB) requirement of Code Section 401(a)(9)(G) and Treasury Regulation 1.401(a)(9)-6, A-1, or any successor regulation thereto.
e. All payments, either in the form of a life annuity or over a period certain must either be nonincreasing or increase only in accordance with the rules set forth in Treasury Regulation 1.401(a)(9)-6, A-1.
f. Unless the participant's interest is distributed in the form of an annuity purchased from an insurance company or in a single sum on or before the required beginning date, as of the first distribution calendar year distributions will be made in accordance with this section 2-151(e). If the participant's interest is distributed in the form of an annuity purchased from an insurance company, distributions thereunder will be made in accordance with the requirements of Code Section 401(a)(9) and the regulations.
For purposes of this section 2-151(e), references to a life annuity shall include an annuity for the joint life expectancy of the participant and the designated beneficiary.
(9) Amount required to be distributed by required beginning date. The amount that must be distributed on or before the participant's required beginning date (or, if the participant dies before distributions begin, the date distributions are required to begin under subsection 2-151(e)(7)(a.) or (b.) is the payment that is required for one payment interval. The second payment need not be made until the end of the next payment interval even if that payment interval ends in the next calendar year. Payment intervals are the periods for which payments are received, e.g., bi-monthly, monthly, semi-annually, or annually. All of the Participant's benefit accruals as of the last day of the first distribution calendar year will be included in the calculation of the amount of the annuity payments for payment intervals ending on or after the participant's required beginning date.
(10) Lump sum distributions. In the case of a lump sum distribution from this plan that is distributed in or after the calendar year in which the participant attains or would have attained age 70½, the amount of the lump sum that equals the participant's or designated beneficiary's required minimum distribution and thus is not an eligible rollover distribution within the meaning of section 2-151(h) of the plan shall be determined using either of the methods set forth in the regulations. The plan administrator shall have the sole discretion to elect the calculation method but shall apply the same method to all lump sum distributions made in the same calendar year.
(11) Incidental death benefit requirement. Any optional form of benefit elected by the participant or designated beneficiary must comply with the minimum distribution incidental benefit requirement of Code Section 401(a)(9)(G). This rule insures that the retirement benefits payable under the plan are more than incidental. If the participant's interest is being distributed in the form of a joint and survivor annuity for the joint lives of the participant and a non-spouse beneficiary, annuity payments to be made on or after the participant's required beginning date to the designated beneficiary after the participant's death must not at any time exceed the applicable percentage of the annuity payment for such period that would have been payable to the participant using the table set forth in Q&A-2 of Section 1.401(a)(9)-6 of the Treasury regulations.
(12) Actuarial increase after age 70½.
a. A participant's accrued benefit shall be actuarially increased to take into account the period after age 70½ in which the employee does not receive any benefits under the plan. The actuarial increase shall commence on April 1 following the calendar year in which the employee attains age 70½, and end on the date on which benefits commence after retirement in an amount sufficient to satisfy Code Section 401(a)(9).
The accrued benefit payable to such a participant as of the end of the period for which the actuarial increase is required shall not be less than:
i. The actuarial equivalent of the employee's accrued benefit as of April 1 of the calendar year following the calendar year in which the Participant attained age 70½, plus
ii. The actuarial equivalent of any additional benefits accrued after the date described in (i) above, less
iii. The actuarial equivalent of any distributions made with respect to the participant's accrued benefit after such date.
b. The actuarial increase described above may reduce the benefit accrual otherwise required under Code Section 411(b)(1)(H)(i).
c. The actuarial adjustment described above shall be made even during a period for which benefits are suspended pursuant to section 2-152.
(13) Plan administrator's discretion. The plan administrator shall have the sole authority and full discretion to apply the provisions of this section 2-151(e) to any benefit option elected by the participant. The plan administrator may, for example, modify a participant's selection of an optional form of benefit to satisfy the incidental death benefit requirement by requiring, at its discretion, that the participant select another form of benefit or another contingent annuitant, or by modifying the form of benefit so that it complies with the applicable rules.
(14) Definitions. The following definitions shall apply to this section 2-151(e) notwithstanding anything contained herein to the contrary.
a. Designated beneficiary. The term "designated beneficiary" shall be determined in accordance with the definition of "beneficiary" in the regulations, notwithstanding that this definition may be different from that set forth elsewhere in this plan, provided that any individual who is a designated beneficiary must also be a beneficiary (but not necessarily all of the Beneficiaries) as defined in this plan. Each Beneficiary, as defined in the plan, however, need not be a designated beneficiary in the event, for example, that a beneficiary disclaims his interest under this plan.
b. Spouse. "Spouse" shall mean "spouse" as defined in the regulations. Nothing in this section 2-151(e) shall be deemed, however, to extend any death benefit or permit any beneficiary designation or payment form not otherwise provided or permitted under this plan.
c. Regulations. "Regulations" shall refer to the Treasury Regulations (including temporary regulations) promulgated under Code Section 401(a)(9), as set forth in Treasury Regulations 1.401(a)(9)-1 through 1.401(a)(9)-6, and any additional guidance issued by the IRS in the form of revenue rulings, notices, other regulations and other guidance published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin or any successor thereto.
d. Distribution calendar year. "Distribution calendar year" is a calendar year for which a minimum distribution is required. For distributions beginning before the participant's death, the first distribution calendar year is the calendar year immediately preceding the calendar year that contains the participant's required beginning date. For distributions beginning after the participant's death, the first distribution calendar year is the calendar year in which distributions are required to begin pursuant to subsection 2-151(e)(7)(i) and (ii).
e. Life expectancy. "Life expectancy" shall mean the period computed by the use of the single life table in section 1.401(a)(9)-9 of the regulations.
(f) Small payments. Effective as to distributions that occur on and after January 1, 2006, if (i) the amount of a distribution is more than $1,000.00, and (ii) the participant does not affirmatively elect to receive the distribution directly or to have such distribution paid directly to an eligible retirement plan pursuant to section 2-151(h), then the plan administrator will pay the distribution in a direct rollover to an individual retirement plan designated by the plan administrator.
(g) Payment to minors and incapacitated persons. (3) By payment in discharge of bills incurred by or for the benefit of such minor or such person. (1) Notwithstanding any provision of the plan to the contrary that would otherwise limit a distributee's election under this section, a distributee may elect, at the time and in the manner prescribed by the plan administrator, to have any portion of an eligible rollover distribution paid directly to an eligible retirement plan specified by the distributee in a direct rollover.
(2) Definitions.
a. Eligible rollover distribution. An eligible rollover distribution is any distribution of all or any portion of the balance to the credit of the distributee, except that an eligible rollover distribution does not include (i) any distribution that is one of a series of substantially equal periodic payments (not less frequently than annually) made for the life (or life expectancy) of the distributee or the joint lives (or joint life expectancies) of the distributee and the distributee's designated beneficiary, or for a specified period of ten years or more; (ii) any distribution to the extent such distribution is required under Code Section 401(a)(9); and (iii) for distributions before January 1, 2002, the portion of any distribution that is not includible in gross income (determined without regard to the exclusion for net unrealized appreciation with respect to employer securities.) The plan administrator may prohibit a distributee's election of a direct rollover with respect to an eligible rollover distribution during the plan year that is less than $200.00. If the distributee elects to have only a portion of an eligible rollover distribution paid to an eligible retirement plan, the plan administrator may require that portion to equal at least $500.00.
b. Eligible retirement plan. An eligible retirement plan is an individual retirement account described in Code Section 408(a), an individual retirement annuity described in Code Section 408(b), an annuity plan described in Code Section 403(a), a qualified trust described in Code Section 401(a), an annuity contract described in Code Section 403(b), and an eligible plan under Code Section 457(b) that is maintained by a state, political subdivision of a state, or any agency or instrumentality of a state or political subdivision of a state that agrees to separately account for amounts transferred into such plan from this plan, provided that such account, annuity, contract, plan or trust accepts the distributee's eligible rollover distribution. Effective as of January 1, 2008, eligible retirement plan shall include a Roth IRA established under Code Section 408A.
c. Distributee. A distributee includes an employee or former employee. In addition, the employee's or former employee's surviving spouse and the employee's or former employee's spouse or former spouse who is an alternate payee under a qualified domestic relations order, as defined in Code Section 414(p), are distributees with regard to the interest of the spouse or former spouse. For distributions on and after January 1, 2007, "distributee" shall include a non-spouse beneficiary of an eligible rollover distribution to the extent permitted by Code Section 402(c)(11).
d. Direct rollover. A direct rollover is a payment by the plan to the eligible retirement plan specified by the distributee.
e. Special rules for rollovers of after-tax contributions. To the extent that an eligible rollover distribution includes amounts that are not includible in gross income (determined without regard to the exclusion for net unrealized appreciation with respect to employer securities), such an amount shall constitute an eligible rollover distribution to the extent that (i) it is transferred in a direct trustee-to-trustee transfer to a qualified trust or to an annuity contract described in Code Section 403(b), and such trust or contract provides for separate accounting for amounts so transferred (and earnings thereon), including separately accounting for the portion of such distribution that is includible in gross income and the portion of such distribution that is not so includible, or (ii) such portion is transferred to an individual retirement account described in Code Section 408(a) or an individual retirement annuity described in Code Section 408(b) (other than an endowment contract).

b. The board of trustees; and

(1) Appoint a plan administrator as set forth in section 2-155(d) it deems appropriate for the proper administration of this plan. In the event that the governing authority has not appointed a plan administrator, the employer shall be the plan administrator.
(2) Appoint a board of trustees to hold and invest the trust fund and to enter into agreements or contracts with the board on such terms and conditions as it deems appropriate. In no event shall the members of the governing authority, members of the plan administrator, or any employee or agent of the employer, other than the board, have any final authority or control over the investment of fund assets.
(3) Amend or terminate the plan as provided in section 2-154 or section 2-156 hereof.
(4) Adopt a funding policy and method to carry out the plan's objectives, the content of which shall be communicated to each member of the board of trustees and all others with discretionary authority over the investment of plan assets.
(5) Periodically review the activities of the board of trustees and investment manager(s). The governing authority shall evaluate the fund's investment performance under such standards as it deems appropriate including the content of the established funding policy and the relative performance of other trustees, investment managers and investment vehicles available for management and investment of qualified plan assets.
(c) The board of trustees. The board of trustees shall be appointed by the governing authority and shall exercise all of the powers and duties assigned to such board as set forth in this section or section 2-158. No individual trustee shall have any responsibilities with respect to the plan other than those set forth herein.
(d) Plan administrator.
(1) The plan administrator shall be the board of trustees. The members shall serve with such compensation for their services as may be established by the employer.
(2) The plan administrator may appoint such agents, as it deems necessary for the effective performance of its duties, and may delegate to such agents the powers and duties, whether ministerial or discretionary, that the plan administrator deems expedient or appropriate. The compensation of such agents shall be fixed by the plan administrator.
(3) Except to the extent that authority is reserved by the Governing Authority, as described in Section 2-155(b) above or to the Board of Trustees as described in Section 2-158, the plan Administrator shall have complete control of the administration of the plan with all powers necessary to enable it to properly carry out the provisions of the plan. The plan Administrator shall have the following specific powers and responsibilities, all of which may be exercised in its sole discretion:
a. To construe the plan and to determine all questions arising in the administration, interpretation and operation of the plan;
b. To decide all questions relating to the eligibility of employees to participate in the benefits of the plan;
c. To determine the benefits of the plan to which any participant, beneficiary or other person may be entitled;
d. To keep records of all acts and determinations of the plan administrator, and to keep all such records, books of accounts, data and other documents as may be necessary for the proper administration of the plan;
e. To prepare and distribute to all plan participants and beneficiaries information concerning the plan and their rights under the plan; and,
f. To do all things it deems necessary or advisable to operate and administer the plan in accordance with its provisions and in compliance with applicable provisions of state and federal law.
(4) To enable the plan administrator to perform its functions, the employer shall supply full and timely information of all matters relating to the compensation and length of service of all eligible employees, their retirement, death or other cause of termination, and such other pertinent facts as the plan administrator may require. The plan administrator shall advise the board of trustees of such facts and issue to the board such instructions as may be required by the board in the administration of the trust fund.
(5) The plan administrator and the employer shall be entitled to rely upon all certificates and reports made by a certified public accountant selected or approved by the employer. The plan administrator, the employer and its officers, and the board, shall be fully protected in respect of any action suffered by them in good faith in reliance upon the advice or opinion of any accountant or attorney, and all action so taken or suffered shall be conclusive upon each of them and upon all other persons interested in the plan or trust.
(e) Standard of fiduciary duty. Any fiduciary, or any person designated by a fiduciary to carry out fiduciary responsibilities with respect to the plan, shall discharge his duties solely in the interests of the participants and beneficiaries for the exclusive purpose of providing them with benefits and defraying the reasonable expenses of administering the plan. Any fiduciary shall discharge his duties with the care, skill, prudence and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent man acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matter would use in the conduct of an enterprise of a like character and with like aims. Any fiduciary shall discharge his duties in accordance with the documents and instruments governing the plan insofar as such documents and instruments are consistent with the provisions of Georgia law.
(f) Claims procedure.
(1) Any participant, beneficiary, or eligible spouse or authorized representative thereof (the "claimant") may file a claim for benefits under the plan by submitting to the plan administrator a written statement describing the nature of the claim and requesting a determination of its validity under the terms of the plan. The plan administrator shall respond to the claimant within a reasonable time.
(2) If the claim is wholly or partially denied, written notice shall be furnished to the claimant, which notice shall set forth in a manner calculated to be understood by the claimant the specific reason or reasons for denial and a specific reference to pertinent plan provisions on which the denial is based.
(3) Any claimant whose claim for benefits has been denied may appeal such denial by resubmitting to the plan administrator a written statement requesting a further review of the decision within a reasonable time after the claimant receives notice of such denial. Such statement shall set forth the reasons supporting the claim, the reasons such claim should not have been denied, and any other issues or comments which the claimant deems appropriate with respect to the claim.
(4) If the claimant shall request in writing, the plan administrator shall make copies of the plan documents pertinent to his claim available for examination of the claimant.
(5) The plan administrator shall review its determination of benefits and the reasons therefor and notify the claimant in writing of its final decision.
(g) Expenses incurred. All fees and expenses reasonably incurred in the administration of the plan, including expenses and fees of the board of trustees shall be treated as expenses of the fund, and paid out of the trust fund, unless paid by the employer.

(b) Incorporation by reference. For purposes of applying such limitations, the following optional provisions shall apply:
(1) The limitation year shall be the plan year.
