(a) Trust fund. There is created a trust fund which consists of contributions made to the plan by the employer and any funds that may be transferred to the plan from funds of other pension plans, as well as the income and return from investment of such contributions and transfers. All contributions and other monies becoming a part of the fund shall be paid to the board of trustees. The board of trustees may appoint a fund custodian, and one or more investment managers or advisors who shall have such powers of investment as are specified from time to time by the board of trustees. All contributions paid over to the plan or the fund shall be invested in accordance with Georgia state law, federal law, and the terms of the plan to which they are contributed.
(b) Trust provisions.
(1) Board of trustees. The members of the board of trustees of the trust fund shall be appointed by the governing authority. The board shall act as a majority but one of more of them may be authorized to sign papers on behalf of all. The board shall consist of five members. To be eligible for membership on the board, a person must be at least 25 years of age and a citizen of the state. Member shall be eligible to succeed themselves only upon appointment. Before taking office, each members appointed shall take an oath to faithfully perform his duties. Appointments shall be for two-year terms to become effective on the July 1 following the date of appointment. Any vacancy occurring on the board prior to the end of the term to which such vacating member was to serve shall be filled by appointment of the governing authority, such newly appointed members to serve for the reminder of the unexpired term of the vacating member.
(2) Duties. The board shall have the following general categories of responsibility as further delineated in section 2-158(e):
a. To invest, manage and control the assets of the plan subject to the appointment of an investments manager as provided in section 2-158(d) of the plan,
b. To pay benefits required to be paid under the plan at the direction of the plan administrator, and,
c. To maintain record and of receipts and disbursements and furnish to the governing authority and/or plan administrator a written annual report.
(3) Authority to delegate duties. The board is authorized to delegate any of its duties, other than those duties relating to the investment or management of the assets of the trust fund, to any individual or organization it deems qualified to perform such duties. The board may employ a bank or trust company under which such bank or trust company shall be the custodian of the fund. The board is only authorized to delegate investment and asset management duties to an investment manager as defined in section 2-158(d). When delegating duties, the board shall document the delegation in either (i) a written amendment to the plan, (iii) minutes or resolutions, or (iii) a separate written agreement.
(4) Institutional trustee. The board may from time to time, with the consent of the governing authority, transfer all or part of the trust fund to a common, collective or pooled trust fund maintained by any institutional trustee, as the board may deem advisable. Any part or all of the trust fund so transferred shall be subject to all the terms and provisions of the common, collective or pooled trust fund that contemplate commingling the plan assets with the assets of other trusts for investment purposes. The board may from time to time, with the consent of the governing authority, withdraw from the common, collective or pooled trust fund all or such part of the trust fund as the board may deem advisable.
(5) Liability limitations. The board shall not be liable for the acts or omissions of parties to whom it has specifically delegated duties, including the making, retention or sale of any investment authorized hereunder nor for a failure to make, retain or sell any investment, except with respect to any acts or omissions in which any trustee participates knowingly or which the any trustee knowingly undertakes to conceal, and which the trustee knows constitutes a breach of fiduciary responsibility. A trustee shall be held harmless by the employer, participant or beneficiary together with his or her heirs, successors and assignees from any and all liability hereunder for acts or omissions performed in good faith and with reasonable prudence. Except as otherwise provided by contract or applicable law, no trustee acting in a fiduciary capacity with respect to the plan shall be liable for any action taken or not taken with respect to the trust and the employer shall indemnify and save each trustee harmless from the effects and consequences of their acts, omissions and conduct in their official capacity, except, if such effects and consequences result from personal gross negligence or willful misconduct.
(c) Investments.
(1) Investment power. The assets of the trust shall be invested by the board in accordance with Georgia law, the terms of the plan and the investment policy developed by the board. Except to the extent such duties specifically are delegated to one or more investment managers under section 2-158(d), the board shall manage and control the assets of the trust fund, including selecting and retaining or disposing of any investment of such assets.
(2) Policies. The board shall establish and comply with investment policies for trust investments. The board shall coordinate its investment and funding policies with the plan's financial needs.
(3) Full investment powers. The board shall have full discretion and authority with regard to the investment of the trust fund, except with respect to plan assets under the control or direction of a properly appointed investment manager. The board is authorized and empowered with all investment powers conferred on trustees of local retirement systems by Georgia law.
(d) Investment managers.
(1) Appointment. The board of trustees may appoint one or more investment managers to manage the assets of all or any of the investment of the trust fund. Each such investment manager shall be either (i) a registered as an investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940; (ii) a bank, as defined in such Act; (iii) or an insurance company qualified to perform the services of investment manager under the laws of more than one state. The board shall obtain from any investment manager a written statement acknowledging that if ERISA applied to the plan, such investment manager would be or on the effective date of its appointment would become a fiduciary within the meaning of ERISA § 3(21)(A) with respect to the trust assets under its management; and certifying that it is either an investment adviser, a bank or an insurance company, which is qualified to be appointed as an investment manager under this plan and trust.
(2) Written agreement. The board shall enter into a written contract or agreement with each such investment manager in connection with its appointment as such, and such contract shall be subject to such terms and conditions and shall grant to the investment manager such authority and responsibilities as the board deems appropriate under the circumstances. The board shall not be responsible for any investment decision made by an investment manager unless the board or an individual trustee actually makes that decision.
(3) Directions. Any investment directions or notifications from an investment manager to the board may be made orally or in writing, or in such manner as shall be agreed upon between the investment manager and the board; provided, in the event the investment manager gives the Board oral recommendations, directions or notifications, the investment manager shall confirm such directions or notifications in writing immediately thereafter.
(4) Violation of board's fiduciary duties. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if, in the board's sole discretion, the execution of any instruction with respect to, or the continued holding of any assets in an investment managed by an investment manager would be in violation of the board's fiduciary responsibilities, the board may refuse to execute such instruction or may dispose of such asset or assets, respectively; provided, the board shall not be responsible for the acts or omissions of such investment manager. In any such case, the board promptly shall notify the investment manager of such situation.
(5) Failure to direct. If an appointed investment manager shall fail to invest all or any portion of the assets under its management, the board shall be responsible for the investment of such assets. If an appointed investment manager shall fail to give the board instructions or directions relating to the voting of shares held pursuant to an investment directed by the investment manager or the execution and delivery of proxies, or relating to the purchase and sale of fractional shares or the exercise of any other ownership right, the board shall take such action as it deems to be in the best interest of the trust, provided such action is consistent with the then existing investment policy statement established by the board.
(6) Termination of appointment. Upon the termination of the appointment of an investment manager, the board may appoint a successor investment manager with respect to the investments formerly under the management of the terminated investment manager or may merge or combine such investments with other investments or trust assets within the guidelines of the investment policy statement.
(7) Asset transfer. If the board directs that an investment manager hold a portion of the assets of the trust as well as make the investment decisions for such fund, the board shall enter into such contractual or other arrangements as are necessary for the transfer and the custody of such assets of the trust fund. If the board terminate such investment manager, it shall take such action to recapture and take directly into the trust fund any assets so transferred.
(8) Reports and valuations. An investment manager who has custody of any portion of the assets of the trust shall keep accurate and detailed books and records on all investments, receipts, disbursements and other transactions for such account and shall determine the fair market value of the assets of such account as of each reporting date, and, further, shall file a copy of such books and records and valuations with the board on or before such deadlines as the board reasonably shall set. The board also shall have the right to request that any person who is responsible for making the investment decisions for an investment account determine the fair market value of any asset, or all of the assets, held for that account and file a copy of such valuation with the board before such deadlines as the board reasonably shall set, and each such person shall comply with any such request.
(e) Powers of the board of trustees.
(1) General authority. Except to the extent such powers are specifically delegated to an investment manager under section 2-158(d) of this plan, the board shall receive, hold, manage, convert, sell, exchange, invest, reinvest, disburse and otherwise deal with the assets of the trust, including contributions to the trust and the income and profits therefrom, without distinction between principal and income and in the manner and for the uses and purposes set forth in the plan and trust.
(2) Specific powers. In the management of the trust, the board or its delegee, as the case may be, shall have the following powers in addition to the powers customarily vested in trustees by state law and in no way in derogation thereof; and such powers shall be exercised in accordance with proper directions and the investment policy statement, the terms of the plan and without order of, or report to, any court:
a. Sales. To sell, exchange, convey, transfer, or otherwise dispose of any property held in the trust, by private contract or at public auction. No person dealing with the board shall be bound to see to the application of the purchase money or other property delivered to the board or to inquire into the validity, expediency, or propriety of any such sale or other disposition.
b. Purchase of property. With any cash at any time held by it, to purchase or subscribe for any authorized investment and to retain the same in trust;
c. Retention of cash. To hold cash without interest in such amounts as may be in its opinion reasonable for the proper operation of the plan and the trust;
d. Exercise of owner's rights. To give general or special proxies or powers of attorney with or without power of substitution with respect to any corporate stock or other security; to exercise any conversion privileges, subscription rights or other options, and to make any payments incidental thereto; to oppose, consent to, or otherwise participate in, reorganizations or other changes affecting any stock, bond, note or other property, and to delegate discretionary powers and pay any assessments or charges, in connection therewith; and generally to exercise any of the powers of an owner, including voting rights, with respect to any stock, bond, note or other property held as part of the trust;
e. Registration of investments. To cause any stock, bond, other security or other property held as part of the trust to be registered in its own name or in the name of one or more of its nominees; provided, the books and records of the board shall at all times show that all such investments are part of the trust;
f. Disbursements. To make disbursements for the payment of benefits under the plan and for the payment of reasonable and proper expenses of the plan or this trust;
g. Retention of disputed funds. To retain any funds or property subject to any dispute without liability for the payment of interest, and to decline to make payment or delivery of the funds or property until final adjudication is made by a court of competent jurisdiction;
h. Execution of instruments. To make, execute, acknowledge and deliver any and all documents of transfer and conveyance and any and all other instruments, which may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the powers herein granted;
i. Settlement of claims and debts. To settle, compromise or submit to arbitration any claims, debts or damages due or owing to or from the trust, to commence or defend suits or legal or administrative proceedings and to represent the trust in all suits and legal and administrative proceedings;
j. Employment of agents, advisers and counsel. To employ and to act or refrain from acting on the advice or opinion of suitable agents, actuaries, accountants, investment advisers, brokers and counsel, and to pay their reasonable expenses and compensation;
k. Power to do any necessary act. To do all acts which it may deem necessary or proper and to exercise any and all powers of the board under the plan upon such terms and conditions as it may deem in the best interests of the plan participants; and
l. Loans. To borrow money only for such periods of time and upon such terms and conditions as the board deems necessary and proper to cover any temporary, short term overdrafts, and to secure such loans by mortgaging, pledging or conveying any property of the trust.
(f) Administration.
(1) Bonds and reports to court. Each member of the board of trustees shall be bonded to the extent required by law, except that, to the extent the requirement of any such bond may be waived, such waiver shall be deemed to have been exercised, and no such bond shall be required. The board shall not be required to make any inventory or appraisal or report to any court or to secure any order of any court for the exercise of any power herein contained.
(2) Accounting by the board. The board, shall cause to be created and maintained adequate and distinct written or computerized records with respect to the operation of the trust, including any and all investments, and any pending litigation to which the plan or the board is a party. Such records shall be retained for so long as the contents thereof may be or become material to the administration of the plan or in the full and complete discharge of liabilities to any and all participants and beneficiaries.
(3) Annual report. The board shall furnish to the governing authority and the plan administrator a written statement of account of the monies in the trust fund each plan year.
(4) Expenses. The expenses incurred by the board in the performance of its duties hereunder, all proper charges and disbursements of the board, including all personal property taxes, income taxes and other taxes of any and all kinds whatsoever, that may be levied or assessed under existing or future laws upon or in respect of the trust or any money, property or security forming a part of the trust fund, may be paid from the trust fund, to the extent not paid by the employer.
(5) Audit. If an audit of the plan's records is required by the state law or by the governing authority for any plan year, the plan administrator shall direct the board to engage an independent qualified public accountant for that purpose, who shall audit the books and records of the plan in accordance with generally accepted accounting standards and furnish a repot of his findings to the plan administrator.
(g) Resignation, removal and succession of trustees.
(1) Resignation. A trustee may resign and become fully discharged from all duties hereunder upon giving 30 days' notice in writing to the governing authority, or such shorter notice as the governing authority.
(2) Removal. A Trustee may be removed at any time by the governing authority by written notice sent to the removed trustee, by registered mail provided at least 30 days prior to its effective date. Possession of all books, documents and monies which are the property of or incident to the fund shall be turned over to the governing authority by any outgoing trustee or trustees.
(3) Successors. Any successor trustee shall, upon appointment and acceptance thereof, become vested with all the property, rights, powers and duties of a trustee hereunder with like effect as if originally named as a trustee.
(h) Prohibited transactions. In no event shall the parties to the plan exercise any powers in a manner that will constitute a prohibited transaction, as defined in Code Section 4975, for which an exemption does not exist.

282:
(a) Headings. The headings and sub-headings in this plan have been inserted for convenience of reference only and are to be ignored in any construction of the provisions hereof.
(b) Action by employer. Any action by the governing authority pursuant to any of the provisions of this plan shall be evidenced by a resolution of its city council certified by the secretary. Any notice, direction, order, request, certification or instruction of the governing authority to the board of trustees or plan administrator shall be in writing and shall be signed either by the city manager or the city secretary. The board of trustees or plan administrator shall be entitled to rely conclusively upon any and all such notices, directions, orders, requests, certifications and instructions received by it from the governing authority, and shall act and be fully protected in acting in accordance therewith.

None of the benefits, payments, proceeds or distributions under this plan shall be subject to the claim of any creditor of any participant or beneficiary, or to any legal process by any creditor of such participant or beneficiary, and none of them shall have any right to alienate, commute, anticipate or assign any of the benefits, payments, proceeds or distributions under this plan except to the extent expressly provided herein to the contrary. Domestic relations orders shall not be recognized. If any participant attempts to dispose of the benefits or the right to receive benefits hereunder, or in the event that there is an effort by a third-party to seize such benefits or the right to receive such benefits by attachment, execution or other legal or equitable process, such right to benefits shall pass and be transferred, at the discretion of the plan administrator, to one or more individuals as may be appointed by the plan administrator from among (i) the beneficiaries, if any, theretofore designated by the participant, or (ii) the eligible spouse, children or other dependents of the participant, in such shares as the plan administrator may appoint. the plan administrator may revoke any appointment so made at any time, and any subsequent appointment by the plan administrator may include the participant.
(d) Qualified military service.
1. Definitions. For the purposes of this section the following definitions shall apply:
i. Differential wage payments mean any payments that are made by the employer to a participant for any period during which the participant is performing military service for more than 30 days and represents all or part of the compensation that the participant would have received from the employer if he or she were performing services for the employer.
ii. Military service means the period of a participant's active duty for training and service in the Army, Navy, Air Force or Marines of the United States of America, the Army National Guard and the Air National Guard when engaged in active duty for training, inactive duty training, or full-time National Guard duty, the commissioned corps of the Public Health Service, and any other category of persons designated by the President in time of war or national emergency.
iii. Qualified military service means military service during which the participant is entitled to reemployment rights under Chapter 43 Title 38 of the United States Code.
iv. USERRA means the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act of 1994.
2. USERRA required service credit. Notwithstanding any provision of the plan to the contrary, contributions, benefits and service credit with respect to qualified military service will be provided in accordance with Code Section 414(u) and USERRA. Plan participants who are reemployed in accordance with the requirements of USERRA shall be treated as not having a break in service during such qualified military service and such periods of qualified military service shall be counted for purposes of vesting and benefit accrual except as provided below.
i. Reemployment. A plan participant must make-up any required participant contributions in order to receive service for benefit accrual under the plan for the period of qualified military service.
ii. Make up contributions. A participant who is required to make-up participant contributions in accordance with this section must do so within the time period the begins on the date he or she returns to employment and ends on the date that is earliest of (i) three times the period of qualified military service; (ii) five years; or (iii) termination of employment. The participant may make-up all or a portion of any required participant contributions and shall receive the amount of service that is directly proportionate to the percentage of participant contributions that are made-up. The participant shall designate the plan year to which such contributions relate. The employer shall grant Service based on the made-up participant contributions in the time and manner as such service is accrued by active participants. Such make-up participant contributions can be paid to the plan in a lump sum, in installments or by payroll deduction.
3. Death during military service. If a participant dies during a period of qualified military service, the participant shall be treated as having returned to employment with the employer on the day before his death and died the next day for purposes of any survivor benefits including pre-retirement survivor benefits and any accelerated vesting. Such participant shall receive service for vesting purposes for the period of qualified military service.
4. Compensation. For purposes of this section, a participant's compensation during the period of qualified military service shall be treated as equivalent to the compensation he or she would have received during such period but for the period of qualified military service. Such determination shall be based on the rate of pay the employee would have received during that time; provided however if the compensation the employee would have received is not reasonably certain, compensation for this purpose shall equal the employee's average compensation during the 12-month period immediately preceding the qualified military service (or, if shorter, the period of employment immediately preceding the qualified military service).
5. Differential wage payments. If the employer pays differential wage payments to the participant while on qualified military leave, such payments shall be treated as compensation under the plan for purposes of benefits and for purposes of Code Section 415 and Section 4.7 of the plan.
(e) Elections by participants. As prescribed by the plan administrator, elections or notifications by participants under this plan may be made either in writing or by electronic means.
(f) Release. Any payment to a participant or beneficiary, or to their legal representatives, in accordance with the provisions of this plan, shall to the extent thereof be in full satisfaction of all claims hereunder against the board, plan administrator and the employer, any of whom may require such participant, beneficiary, or legal representative, as a condition precedent to such payment, to execute a receipt and release therefor in such form as shall be determined by the board, the plan administrator, or the employer, as the case may be.
(g) Complaint with applicable laws. The employer, through the board and plan administrator, shall interpret and administer the plan in such manner that the plan shall remain in compliance with the Code, laws of the State of Georgia, and all other applicable laws, regulations, and rulings.
(h) Merger. In the event of any merger or consolidation of the plan with any other plan, or the transfer of assets or liabilities by the plan to another plan, each participant must receive (assuming that the plan would terminate) the benefit immediately after the merger, consolidation, or transfer which is equal to or greater than the benefit such participant would have been entitled to receive immediately before the merger, consolidation, or transfer (assuming that the plan had then terminated).
(i) Governing law. The plan shall be governed by the laws of the State of Georgia, without regard to its conflicts of laws principles, to the extent that such laws are not preempted by federal law.
(j) Location of participant or beneficiary unknown. In the event that all or any portion of the distribution payable to a participant or his beneficiary shall remain unpaid solely by reason of the plan administrator's inability to ascertain the whereabouts of such participant or beneficiary, the amount unpaid shall be forfeited. However, such forfeiture shall not occur until five years after the amount first became payable. The plan administrator shall make a diligent effort to locate the participant or beneficiary including the mailing of a registered letter, return receipt requested, to the last known address of such participant or beneficiary. In the event a participant or beneficiary is located subsequent to his benefit being forfeited, such benefit shall be restored and distributed.
(k) Use of electronic communication.
(1) Notwithstanding anything contained herein to the contrary, where this plan or the plan administrator requires that communications regarding the plan from a participant or beneficiary be made in writing to the employer or any other entity, such communications may be made in any means prescribed by the plan administrator. The plan administrator shall designate acceptable means of communication by distributing (or directing the distribution of) instructions, personal identification numbers, telephone numbers, website addresses or similar information that will enable the participant or beneficiary to use such alternate means of communication. Where the plan administrator does not prescribe an alternate means of communication, such communications must be made in writing and delivered to the plan administrator via hand delivery or mail. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the plan administrator may prescribe that certain types of communications shall be made exclusively by telephone or electronically. In such a case, the plan administrator may not accept the written communication, or may delay the acceptance or implementation of the communication, as it deems appropriate.
(2) The plan administrator may communicate with the employees, participants and beneficiaries concerning this plan using such electronic means as it deems appropriate, provided that such use is, in the judgment of the plan administrator, consistent with the Code.
(l) Participant obligation to advise of mailing address.
(1) Each participant and, in the case of a deceased participant, his beneficiary, shall keep the plan administrator apprised of his current mailing address. Any notice from the participant or beneficiary changing his mailing address shall be in writing and directed to the individual, position or department within the plan administrator that is responsible for maintaining records regarding the plan and its participants. Any such notice shall include sufficient information from which the plan Administrator can verify the identity of the participant or beneficiary who provided the notice. If the plan administrator receives a change of address request and believes that it may not have been made by or on behalf of the participant or beneficiary, the plan administrator shall take reasonable steps to verify the address. If the plan administrator cannot verify the address or the identity of the individual who submitted the address change, it shall take any steps it deems necessary or appropriate to ensure to protect the participant or beneficiary and the plan.
2. Any notice sent by the plan administrator to the participant's or beneficiary's mailing address, as such address is reflected on the plan administrator's records, shall be deemed to have been provided to the participant or beneficiary, as applicable, regardless of whether it is actually received. Nothing in this paragraph 2-159(l) shall be deemed to relieve the plan administrator of any obligation to use a good faith effort to contact a participant or beneficiary or to contradict the procedures set forth in Section 2-159(j), "location of participant or beneficiary unknown."

It is essential to the proper administration and operation of the city that all elected or appointed city officials be, and give the appearance of being, independent and impartial; that public office not be used for private gain; and that there be public confidence in the integrity of the governing authority. The governing authority finds that the public interest requires that they protect against such conflicts of interest by establishing appropriate ethical standards with respect to the conduct of the members of the governing authority in situations where a conflict may exist.
The purpose of this code of ethics is to:
(1) Encourage high ethical standards in official conduct by city officials;
(2) Establish guidelines for ethical standards of conduct for all such officials by setting forth those acts or actions that are incompatible with the interest of the city;
(3) Require disclosure by such officials of private financial or other interest in matters affecting the city; and,
(4) Serve as a basis for disciplining those who refuse to abide by its terms.
The provisions of this code of ethics shall be applicable to all elected or appointed city officials.
Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, state law and the Charter of the city shall be controlling in the event of an actual conflict with the provisions of this code of ethics. This article shall be interpreted to supplement, and not replace, said provisions of state law and the Charter.

(a) No application for a license hereunder shall be granted where the application, investigation or the evidence presented to the city manager shows any of the following conditions to exist:
(1) The applicant or any person owning a direct or indirect beneficial interest in the license for which application is made lacks sufficient mental or physical capacity to conduct the business for which application has been made, or has been dishonorably discharged from the armed services of the United States.
(2) The applicant or any person having direct or indirect beneficial interest in the issuance of the license has had any license issued by the city or by any other city in the state or by any other licensing authority in the state relating to the manufacture, distribution, or sale of alcoholic beverages previously suspended or revoked.
(3) The applicant as a previous holder of a license to sell alcoholic beverages has violated any law, regulation, or ordinance relating to such business within a five-year period immediately preceding the date of the application for license hereunder.
(4) Any applicant for a retail license hereunder is related to any licensed distributor or wholesaler of alcoholic beverages in the city within the first degree of consanguinity or affinity as computed according to state law.
(5) The applicant is under 21 years of age.
(6) The applicant is not a lawful permanent resident or citizen of the United States as verified by the production of one of the following:
a. A Permanent Resident Card, commonly known as a Green Card, indicating permanent, not conditional, residence; or
b. A valid and unexpired passport with an "1-551" Stamp; or
c. A birth certificate showing birth in the United States; or a Certificate of Naturalization; or
d. A Certificate of Citizenship; or
e. A Report of Birth Abroad of United States Citizen as reported on a Form F-240 as no exist or as hereafter amended or superseded; or
f. A valid and unexpired U.S. Passport.
(7) The applicant does not reside and maintains his primary place of residence for voting purposes in Colquitt County, Georgia as verified by the production of one of the following"
a. A valid State of Georgia issued Driver's License;
b. A valid State of Georgia issued Identification Card;
c. A valid Motor Vehicle Registration;
d. Proof of ownership of a primary residence in Colquitt County, Georgia along with a valid Homestead Exemption for said property; or
e. A valid and current Colquitt County Voter Registration Card.
(8) Proof of citizenship and residency pursuant to subparagraphs (6) and (7) of this section shall be submitted with any application for a license.
(9) For the purposes of this subsection, temporary visas, work visas, or any other similar documents, other than those listed in subsection (a)(6), are not acceptable.
(b) When contrary to the public interest or welfare, no license shall be issued to:
(1) Any person is determined by the city manager, by reason of that person's business experience, financial standing, trade associations, personal associations, records of arrest, or reputation in the community in which he has resided, who is not likely to maintain the operation for which he is seeking a license in conformity with federal, state, or local laws.
(2) Any entity or person having any interest therein, either as owner, partner, stockholder, or otherwise having a direct or indirect beneficial or absolute interest, shall have been convicted of any felony under the laws of this state or of the United States within a period of ten years immediately preceding the date of receipt of the application. The term "conviction" shall include an adjudication of guilt or a plea of guilty or a plea of nolo contendere or the forfeiture of a bond by a person charged with a crime.
(3) Any person has been convicted of a misdemeanor, or ordinance violation, or traffic offense involving moral turpitude, alcoholic beverages, or controlled substances, within five years immediately preceding the date of receipt of the application.
(4) Any location at which a license has previously been suspended or revoked by either the city or the Georgia Department of Revenue and where, in the opinion of the city manager, there exists the likelihood that the utilization of such license at such location would cause or necessitate greater than normal police activity, observation or inspection in order to either prevent violation of laws and regulations relating to such location or to maintain public order, due to the history of either:
a. Violations of the provisions of this chapter or of the laws, rules and regulations of the state relative to alcoholic beverages by the holder of the previous license at such location or agents, servants or employees thereof; or
b. Activities or conduct of patrons of the business in which such previous license was utilized at such location, all as compared to the locations of other licensed premises, or would cause or tend to cause, in the opinion of the city manager, greater than normal community problems or conflict as compared to the locations of other licensed premises; or
c. Any location at which a license has previously been suspended or revoked by either the city or the Georgia Department of Revenue and where, in the opinion of the city manager, problems associated with the utilization of a prior license at such location were such that it would not be in the best interest of the public health, safety or welfare to grant any other license for such location.
(c) In determining whether to issue a license, the city manager shall, in addition to other provisions of this chapter, consider all information that would be considered by him in any revocation or suspension hearing or license renewal hearing.
(d) Notwithstanding the foregoing, the city manager, in his sole discretion, may decide to authorize the issuance of a license to a person who has in the past been convicted of, plead guilty to, entered a plea of nolo contendere to, or forfeited a bond on any crime when, after a thorough investigation of all the facts including parole or probation officer's reports, judge's recommendations, and any other evidence bearing on the character of the applicant, it has determined, in the sole discretion of the city manager, that such action is in keeping with the ends of justice and the public interest and welfare.
(e) The citizenship and residency requirements contained in this chapter are required to be met at the time of application and during the license period. Any application or license holder shall submit proof thereof in the forms set forth in section 6-32(a)(6)c. through f. at any time requested by the City of Moultrie.
(f) Where the applicant is a corporation, a stockholder having a majority interest therein must meet the requirements contained herein, and the license shall be issued jointly to the corporation and such stockholder. If the applicant is a partnership, the requirements contained herein shall be met by one of the partners having a majority interest, whether general or limited. However, any applicant for a packaged spirituous liquor license shall be required to designate a resident of the city who shall be responsible for any matter relating to the license.
